sections.text: We rolled back the search change on 3 May after 40 minutes, and the rollback took longer than the incident would have.
Reverting the deploy was two minutes. Undoing the index migration it had already run was 34, and we did it by hand under pressure at midnight.
Everyone knows a rollback plan is not a plan until it has been run. Almost nobody runs it, because running it costs a scheduled outage to fix a problem that has not happened.
The only rollback procedures I have seen work on the night are the ones that were exercised on an afternoon when nothing was wrong.
So I think the rule is not write a rollback plan. It is that a rollback plan you have never executed should be assumed not to exist, and planned around accordingly.
